profile.entities: Sarda Energy & Minerals Ltd (Parent); Sarda Metals & Alloys Ltd; SKS Power Generation Chhattisgarh Ltd; Adishankar Khuitam Power Pvt Ltd
profile.subseg: Thermal Power (Merchant/PPA); Hydropower; Coal Mining; Iron Ore Pellets; Sponge Iron; HB Wire
profile.themes: Energy Security & Atmanirbhar Bharat; Thermal Capacity Doubling (SKS); Coal Mine Expansion; Steel Cycle Bottoming; PPA Mix Shift

bull_bear.body: Net cash positive standalone; Consolidated liquidity INR 2,380 cr. Record 200% dividend recommended. Strategic M&A: Acquired majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam (66 MW Hydro). Treasury: Minor Godawari Power share purchase (<1% of liquidity) deemed normal treasury ops, no major stake buildup planned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical: West Asia/Middle East conflict impacting oil prices, inflation, and global steel demand. Regulatory: Delays in environment clearances for SKS expansion and new mines. Market: Chinese steel export dumping (though safeguard measures in place); Volatility in merchant power prices. Operational: Seasonal hydro variability; Execution delays in brownfield expansions.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and transformational; Emphasizes shift from cyclical commodity player to stable energy-mining integrated model. Prudent on steel cycle (believes bottomed out but wary of global war impact). Aggressive on capacity doubling with strong balance sheet support.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management is exploring demerger/separation of the Renewable Energy business specifically, not the entire power vertical. Pellet capex revival is strategically timed to coincide with state-owned (CMDC) iron ore mine auctions in Chhattisgarh over next 2-2.5 years, securing raw material for expanded capacity.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Net debt-free balance sheet and comfortable liquidity driven by strong cash generation to support scalable growth', reiterated by the MD as the basis for quadrupling mining and doubling energy capacity.
- Credit profile: SEML parent rated CRISIL AA- / Positive / A1+ (reaffirmed Nov-2025), SMAL (ferro alloys subsidiary) CRISIL A / Positive / A1, Chhattisgarh Hydro Power LLP ICRA A+ / Stable, Madhya Bharat Power Corporation IND A+ / Stable / A1; outlook changed to Positive.
- Deck flags a 'Long term credit rating upgrade to AA- in FY26 from A in FY21 with a strong liquidity position of Rs. 2,380 cr'.
- Consolidated TOL/NW of 0.56, 0.5, 0.58, 0.52 and 0.49 with Net Debt/EBITDA of 0.90, 1.39, 1.10, 0.10 and (0.03) across the Mar-23 to Jun-26 points shown - i.e. leverage has moved to a net cash position at the latest point.
- 'Highest Ever Dividend in FY26' at Rs 2.00 per share, up a rising series from FY22; FY23 additionally carried a special dividend on account of the golden jubilee year.
- Roadmap pairs capital optimisation with 'Maintain disciplined project execution and timely commissioning'.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Energy (2/3 of EBITDA): Thermal gen 4,155 MU (+84% YoY); Hydro 661 MU (+31% YoY). Mining: Gare Palma IV/7 hit max limit 1.8 MTPA; Shahpur West commissioning FY27. Metals: Pellets 0.83 MT (record); Sponge Iron 0.35 MT (record); HB Wire 40k MT (record).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising power demand (270 GW peak) and need for domestic coal security amid import disruptions | NTPC Ltd | beneficiary | High | Sector tailwinds for domestic thermal generators with coal linkages; Sarda's own expansion validates the thermal renaissance theme. |
| Steel cycle bottoming out and potential infrastructure rebuild post-Iran/US deal | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Med | Long product price recovery benefits integrated players; Sarda's view on bottoming supports broader sector recovery thesis. |
| Volatility in merchant power prices pushing IPPs toward PPA models | JSW Energy | beneficiary | Med | Sarda's shift to 300MW PPA mirrors industry move to visibility; benefits peers with similar mixed-portfolio strategies. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Three-vertical integrated model: Energy (thermal, hydro, solar), Minerals (iron ore mine, coal mines, washery) and Value-Added Metals (steel products, ferro alloys).
- Energy is the declared earnings engine, though the deck states its contribution two ways: 'Energy Segment contributed nearly 70% to consol EBITDA' (Q1 FY27 highlights) and 'Contributes approximately two-thirds of consolidated EBITDA' (business overview) - both readings are quoted as given.
- Transformation arc set out as FY21 'Cyclical, Commodity-Driven Business' with earnings tied to steel/ferro alloy price volatility and sensitivity to Chinese markets, to FY22-25 'Diversification into Energy & Significant Capacity Addition', to FY26 'Geared up for next phase of growth'.
- Metals business claims to be 'Positioned in the lowest quartile of the steel cost curve' with proximity to end-markets supporting competitive delivered pricing.
- Stated value creation since FY21: '2x jump in Revenue from Rs. 2,343 cr in FY21 to Rs 5,928 cr in FY26; CAGR of 20%', '3x jump in EBITDA from Rs. 664 cr in FY21 to Rs 2,025 cr in FY26', '3x jump in PAT from Rs. 376 cr in FY21 to Rs 1,109 cr in FY26' and '5x jump in energy capacity from 191 MW in FY21 to 929 MW in FY26'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] SKS Power, an operational 2x300 MW thermal plant in Chhattisgarh, was acquired under IBC on 21st Aug 2024; FY26 brought 'Successful integration; SC ratification for SKS Power Acquisition' and 'Dismissal of all pending appeals against SEML's resolution plan removes overhang'.
- [Regulatory one-off] Q1 FY27 net profit includes a one-time net benefit of Rs. 110 crore relating to regulatory approval of the final project cost for the 113 MW Sikkim hydropower plant - the deck flags this as the partial support for its highest-ever quarterly PAT.
- [Sector tailwinds] Deck leans on Viksit Bharat 2047 manufacturing/semiconductor demand, Atmanirbhar Bharat energy security, government push on coal gasification, and the National Electricity Plan's ~900 GW installed capacity by FY32 (around 596 GW renewable and 304 GW conventional).
- [Ownership] Shareholding as on 30-Jun-2026: Promoters 73%, Institutions 7%, Non-institutions 20%; market cap Rs 18,118 Cr on 35.2 Cr shares at CMP Rs 514.7 (BSE) as on 31st July 2026, face value Rs 1.00.
- [Board] Eleven-member board listed with five committees (Audit, CSR, NRC, Stakeholder Relationship, Risk Management), chaired by Kamal Kishore Sarda with Pankaj Sarda as MD and Padam Kumar Jain as Director & CFO; several independent directors are former CMDs of PFC, CSPTCL and CMPDI.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Thermal realization >INR 5/unit; Q4 exchange price ~INR 3.75/unit. Coal index up 8-9% YoY due to import disruptions/West Asia crisis. Iron ore prices softening (NMDC/OMC cuts) offsetting coal cost pressure for steel segment. PPA mix shift expected to stabilize realizations vs merchant volatility.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Driven by efficiency gains, full-year Rehar hydro, and solar commissioning in FY27; Margins: Stability expected via shift to 300MW medium/long-term PPAs (up from 100MW); Order Inflow: Secured 300MW PPA capacity for next year; Capex: INR 500-700 cr annually for FY27-28 (excl. SKS expansion); SKS expansion capex TBD pending DPR, commissioning targeted FY30-31.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Power sales mix shifting: FY26 mostly merchant (short-term); FY27 guidance sees 200-300MW under medium/long-term PPAs providing visibility vs volatile spot prices (spot ~INR 3.75/unit in Q4).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) SKS Power brownfield expansion to 1,200 MW by FY30 (land/fuel ready, EC pending); 2) Coal mine capacity quadrupling (Shahpur West, Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga, Senduri); 3) Hydropower pipeline: 66 MW (Arunachal) + 74 MW (Chhattisgarh) + 25 MW (Rehar operational); 4) Pellet plant expansion (0.9 to 2.0 MTPA) to capture new Chhattisgarh iron ore mines.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sarda Energy has successfully pivoted from a cyclical steel player to an integrated energy-mining major, with FY26 EBITDA tripling to INR 2,025 cr driven by a 84% surge in thermal generation and record coal output. The strategic roadmap focuses on doubling thermal capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 and quadrupling mining capacity, while re-entering steel capex (pellet expansion) to capture upcoming iron ore supply in Chhattisgarh.
